newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-CAVALIERS BEAT MAGIC EQUALLING BEST DEFENSIVE EFFORT EVER.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-CAVALIERS BEAT MAGIC EQUALLING BEST DEFENSIVE EFFORT EVER.

text.p: The Cleveland Cavaliers matched the best defensive effort in NBA history Wednesday when they beat the Orlando Magic 84-57.

The Cavaliers, who lead the league in fewest points allowed per game this season, tied a mark that was set by the Boston Celtics against the Milwaukee Hawks in the first season of the shot clock, 1955, and was equalled last season by the Miami Heat against the Philadelphia 76ers.
"We did a lot of things right," Cleveland coach Mike Fratello said. "We were good defensively. We were sharp."
The Magic's previous low output was 76, most recently in a three-point win at Indiana on November 23.
Terrell Brandon scored 22 points and added eight assists and five steals for the Cavaliers, who snapped a five-game losing streak at Orlando dating back to 1994.
The Magic, without injured starters Penny Hardaway, Nick Anderson and Dennis Scott, fell to 4-5 at home after going 37-4 at Orlando Arena last season.
"Fifty-seven points or whatever, we knew we were in the vicinity," Wilkins said. "Man, it was wild out there tonight. We played against a good defensive team."
The Magic shot just 34 percent (21-of-62) while the Cavaliers shot 45 percent (33-of-73). Cleveland has allowed less than 75 points seven times in 16 games this season.
In Houston, Charles Barkley had 19 points and 27 rebounds and the Rockets held the Boston Celtics to two points in the final 6:56 en route to a 94-89 victory.

Rockets All-Star centre Hakeem Olajuwon returned to the lineup after he was hospitalized for the second time this season with an irregular heartbeat. He has missed four games this season with the ailment.
"I feel normal. I was winded, but that's part of the game," said Olajuwon, who had 16 points, seven rebounds and five blocks in 40 minutes.
At Utah, Karl Malone 26 points and the Jazz allowed just 27 points in the middle two periods for a 101-75 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers, their 12th straight win.
John Stockton added 18 points for the Jazz, two wins shy of their franchise record of 14 set in the 1994-95 season.
Shaquille O'Neal scored 21 for Los Angeles.
In Detroit, Terry Mills scored 14 of his season-high 25 points in the fourth quarter and Grant Hill came within two assists of a triple-double as the Pistons beat the Atlanta Hawks 100-90.
Hill had 22 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists, while Joe Dumars chipped in 22 points and seven assists for Detroit.
"That was the best basketball I've seen two teams play here this season," said Detroit coach Doug Collins. "Both teams executed. We just finally got them to miss some shots at the end."
In Miami, Tim Hardaway scored a season-high 33 points as the Heat extended their franchise-record winning streak to nine games, 101-79 over the Dallas Mavericks.
Miami, which never trailed, improved to 8-0 against Western Conference foes. Dallas has dropped seven of its last eight road games.
At New Jersey, Patrick Ewing scored 11 of his 30 points in the fourth quarter and led the New York Knicks to a 109-102 victory over the Nets.
Ewing scuffled with 7-foot-6 (2.29 metres) Nets centre Shawn Bradley in the last minute after New York had rallied to take the lead.
Former Net Buck Williams also scored 11 points in the fourth quarter, when the Knicks scored 37 points and erased a six-point deficit.
Robert Pack and Kendall Gill scored 20 points apiece for the Nets, who have lost four of their last five.
In Phoenix, A.C. Green scored a season-high 21 points and grabbed 12 rebounds as the Suns beat the Golden State Warriors 118-87 for just their second win of the season.
The Suns used a 31-7 run to open a 37-17 lead. The point totals were a season-high for the Suns and a season-low by a Phoenix opponent in an opening quarter.
Michael Finley also had 21 points and Danny Manning added 20 as the Suns posted their second straight home win.

In San Antonio, Avery Johnson recorded 24 points and 11 assists and Dominique Wilkins added 24 and 10 rebounds off the bench as the Spurs snapped an eight-game losing streak with a 113-103 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers.
Rookie Allen Iverson had 26 points and 11 assists, while Derrick Coleman added 21 and 12 rebounds for Philadelphia.
In Vancouver, Reggie Miller scored 31 of his season-high 36 points in the first half to lead the Indiana Pacers to the biggest win in franchise history, 127-80 over the Grizzlies.

Vancouver has dropped five straight. The Grizzlies, playing without starters Greg Anthony, Blue Edwards and Bryant Reeves due to injuries, fell two points shy of the worst-ever loss in their young history.
